content: Inflammation is a critical factor in the development and progression of bronchiectasis. Two small studies have suggested that inhaled corticosteroids may provide limited benefits, and oral corticosteroids could potentially be beneficial in managing bronchiectasis. The objective of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness of oral corticosteroids in both acute exacerbations and stable phases of bronchiectasis. To achieve this, the Cochrane Airways Group Specialised Register was thoroughly searched, and the bibliographies of relevant studies were reviewed. The search was up-to-date as of May 2011. Only randomised controlled trials (RCTs) were considered eligible for inclusion in this review. However, no randomised controlled trials meeting the inclusion criteria were identified during the search process. As a result, there is no high-quality evidence from RCTs to support or refute the use of oral corticosteroids in the treatment of either acute exacerbations or stable bronchiectasis. In conclusion, due to the lack of randomised trials, no definitive recommendations can be made regarding the use of oral corticosteroids for managing bronchiectasis in either its acute or stable forms.
